steps.html:
Fractions ↔ Decimals ↔ Percents

14 = 0.25 = 25%

Three ways to write the same amount.

fraction → decimaltop ÷ bottom
decimal → percent× 100 (decimal 2 places right)
percent → decimal÷ 100 (decimal 2 places left)
say: Today: fractions, decimals and percents. One fourth, zero point two five, and twenty-five percent.
They're three ways to write the very same amount.
Fraction to decimal: divide the top by the bottom. Decimal to percent: move the decimal two places right. Percent to decimal: two places left.

steps.html:
Know these by heart

1250%1425%3475%1520%1812.5%1333⅓%11010%

Eighths: 58 = 5 × 12.5% = 62.5%.
say: Memorize these: one half, fifty percent. One fourth, twenty-five. Three fourths, seventy-five. One fifth, twenty. One eighth, twelve and a half. One third, thirty-three and a third. One tenth, ten.
Then build from them. Five eighths is five times twelve and a half, sixty-two and a half percent.
Write five eighths as a percent.
steps.okSay: Yes! Five eighths is sixty-two and a half percent.
steps.noSay: Not quite. One eighth is twelve and a half percent, so five eighths is sixty-two and a half percent.

steps.html:
Decimal → fraction: read it out loud

0.14 = “fourteen hundredths” = 14100
simplify: 750
4% = 0.04 (not 0.4!)
say: To turn a decimal into a fraction, read it out loud.
Zero point one four is fourteen hundredths, fourteen over one hundred.
Simplify by dividing both by two: seven fiftieths.
Careful with small percents. Four percent is zero point zero four, not zero point four.

steps.okSay: Yes! Zero point six is sixty percent, the biggest.
steps.no: Turn all into percents: 0.6 = 60%, 58%, 59 ≈ 55.6%, 47 ≈ 57.1%. The greatest is 0.6.
steps.noSay: Not quite. Turn them all into percents: sixty, fifty-eight, about fifty-five point six, and about fifty-seven point one. Zero point six is the greatest.

say: Great! Now 4 practice questions. You'll see the answer and an explanation after each one.
Last part: three checkpoint questions. Get two out of three to finish the lesson. You've got this!

steps.html:
Remember

1. Fraction → decimal: top ÷ bottom.

2. Decimal ↔ percent: move the decimal 2 places.

3. Memorize ½, ¼, ¾, ⅕, ⅛, ⅓.

4. To compare, turn everything into the same form.
say: Let's review. Fraction to decimal: divide top by bottom.
Decimal and percent: move the decimal two places.
And to compare, turn them all into the same form. Nice work!
